2.1.	 QUALITY CONTROL TESTS FOR RADIOGRAPHERS
2.1.2.2.	 Equipment
The equipment needed for the test is a long ruler or a measuring tape at 
least 100 cm long.
2.1.2.3.	 Procedure
The following procedure is used for the test:
(a)	
Set an SID of 100 cm by using the SID indicator of the system.
(b)	
Measure the actual SID using the ruler or measuring tape, starting at 
the focal spot indicator on the side of the X  ray tube and extending 
to the tabletop or surface of the image receptor (Fig. 3). 	

Note: Some recent X ray systems do not have an indicator of the focal spot. 
In this case, the manufacturer’s documentation could be used as a reference 
to estimate its position, or the medical physicist may determine the location 
of the focal spot using the intercept theorem.
(c)	
Record the result.
2.1.2.4.	 Analysis and interpretation
Compare the measured value with the SID readout indicator of 
the X ray system.

2.1.2.3. Procedure
The following procedure is used for the test:
(a) Set an SID of 100 cm by using the SID indicator of the system.
(b) Measure the actual SID using the ruler or measuring tape, starting at the focal spot indicator on the side of the X ray tube and extending to the tabletop or surface of the image receptor (Fig. 3).
Note: Some recent X ray systems do not have an indicator of the focal spot. In this case, the manufacturer’s documentation could be used as a reference to estimate its position, or the medical physicist may determine the location of the focal spot using the intercept theorem.
(c) Record the result.
2.1.2.4. Analysis and interpretation
Compare the measured value with the SID readout indicator of the X ray system.

visual_relations: Figure 3 shows a vertical schematic: X-ray tube labeled 'Focus' at top, with a built-in measuring tape extending downward through the tube housing; a yellow dashed line represents the central ray from the focal spot to the tabletop; a separate measuring tape lies horizontally on the tabletop; two circular magnified insets show scale markings: left inset shows '0' near the focal spot indicator, right inset shows '99' near the tabletop surface, indicating a measured distance close to 100 cm. Arrows label 'Built-in measuring tape', 'Table', and 'Measuring tape'.
units: cm
uncertainties: The note indicates uncertainty in focal spot location for modern systems lacking a physical indicator; alternative methods (manufacturer docs, intercept theorem) are suggested but no numerical uncertainty bounds are provided.
summary: This section describes a quality control test to verify Source-to-Image Distance (SID) accuracy in X-ray systems. It specifies required equipment (≥100 cm ruler/tape), step-by-step procedure (set SID to 100 cm via system indicator, then physically measure from focal spot indicator to image receptor surface), and analysis (compare measured vs. indicated SID). Figure 3 illustrates the measurement setup, showing alignment of focal spot, central ray, and measurement tapes, with scale insets suggesting a reading near 99 cm.

2.1.2.1.	 Description and objective
The aim of this test is to determine the accuracy of the SID indicator of 
the X ray system. This test has an important role for radiographic imaging and 
when dose monitoring software is used, as the distance indication may be used 
as an input for determining the distance from the focal spot to the entrance 
surface (skin) [4].
